brief: The oldest surviving German half-timber (Fachwerkbau) house in the Freistadt area, c.1845 with changes c.1870 and c.1890: a storey-and-a-half gabled block with its timber frame and whitewashed nogging exposed, a sagging roof of old shingles, later sash windows, a small gabled entry vestibule and a lower rear addition, overgrown with weeds and shrubs.

facade.notes: the Hilgendorf House (Freistadt WI, c.1845): a Pomeranian Fachwerk house, the timber frame filled with clay-and-straw nogging under plaster, part of its weatherboarding gone, a small frame entry shed; weeds and lilacs; derelict

why.note: Freistadt: the first German Lutheran settlement in Wisconsin, Fachwerk houses
